translations.text: In the beginning God made heaven and earth.
The earth was not visible and was not yet formed. Darkness was over the deep, and the Spirit of God hovered over the water.
And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light Day and the darkness Night. Night came, and morning dawned, and there was one day.
God said, “Let there be an expanse in the midst of the water to separate the waters.” And it was so.
God made the expanse, and God separated the water below the expanse from the water above the expanse.
God called that expanse Heaven, and God saw that it was good. Night came, and morning dawned, and there was a second day.
God said, “Let the water below heaven gather into one place, and let dry land appear.” And it was so. The water gathered into its gathering places, and dry land appeared.
And God called the dry land Earth, and he called the gathered waters Sea. And God saw that it was good.

God said, “Let the earth sprout green vegetation: plants that produce seed, each according to its seed, its kind, and its likeness, and trees that bear and produce fruit with seed inside it, which comes forth according to its kind upon the earth.” And it was so.

The earth brought forth green vegetation, [plants] producing seed according to their kinds and their forms, and trees bearing and producing fruit with seed inside it, according to their kinds upon the earth. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening, and morning came, and it was the third day.
God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth and to separate day from night. Let them serve as signs and mark seasons, days, and years.
Let them provide light in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
And God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the smaller light to rule the night, together with its stars.
And God placed them in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth.
And to rule over the day and the night and to separate the night from the light. And God saw that it was good.
Night came, and morning dawned, and there was a fourth day.
And God said, “Let the water bring forth moving creatures that have the breath of life, and birds that fly above the earth and below heaven.” And it was so.

God made the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, which the water brought forth according to their kinds, and every flying bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth, and let the birds multiply on the earth.”
Night came, and morning dawned, and there was a fifth day.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth kinds of livestock, moving creatures, and wild animals of the earth, each according to its kind.” And it was so.
God made livestock according to their kinds, [and everything that moves on the earth according to its kind, and the wild animals of the earth according to their kinds.] And God saw that it was good.

God said, “Let us make humankind in our image and according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the wild animals of the earth, the birds of heaven, the livestock, all the earth, and the animals that move upon the earth.”
God made humankind in the likeness of God; male and female he made them.

God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and take possession of it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, all livestock, and everything that moves upon the earth.”

God said, “Look, I have given you every plant that produces seed and sprouts from its seed when sown upon all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed that can be sown. These are food for you;
and for all the wild animals of the earth, all the birds of heaven, and everything that moves on the earth that has the breath of life, let all green plants be food for you.” And it was so.
God saw everything he had made, and it was very good. Night came, and morning dawned, and there was a sixth day.
Heaven and earth were completed.
God finished making the whole world, his work, and on the seventh day God rested from all his work.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work that God had begun to do.
This is the book of the creation of heaven and earth, when they came into being, on the day when God made heaven and earth.
And every plant [of the field, before it existed on the earth, and every plant] of the earth, before it sprouted—for God had not sent rain upon the earth before a human being was created.
But only a spring of water rose from the earth [and watered the dry land].
God made the man from the dust of the earth and breathed the breath of life into his face, and the man became a living being.
God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and placed there the man whom he had made.

God also caused every tree that was good for food and pleasing to look at to grow from the earth, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree that reveals and gives understanding of good and evil.
A river flows out from his presence to water the garden, and from there it divides toward the four corners of the world.
The name of the first river is Pishon. [It is] the one that goes around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
The gold of that land is good, and there are shining gems and green gems there.
The name of the second river is Gihon. It is the one that goes around the whole land of Ethiopia.
The third river is the Tigris, which flows through Persia, and the fourth river is the Euphrates.
God took the man whom he had made and placed him in the garden to cultivate it and guard it.
And God commanded Adam and said to him, “Eat from every tree that is in the garden.”
But you must not eat from the tree that gives understanding of good and evil, because on the day you eat from it, you will certainly die.
And God said, “It is not good for the man to live alone. Let us make him a companion who will help him.”

God also made the wild animals from the earth (all the wild animals) and all the birds of the sky, and brought them to Adam to see what he would name them. Whatever Adam named each living being would be its name.
Adam gave all their names to the livestock, the birds of the sky, and all the wild animals. But for Adam no helper like him was found.
God sent sleep upon Adam, and he slept. God took one of his ribs and filled its place with flesh.
God built up the rib that he had taken from Adam, made it into a woman, and brought her to Adam.
Adam said, “This is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. She shall be my wife, because she came out of [?].”
For this reason a man leaves his father and mother and joins himself to his wife, and the two become one flesh.
And Adam and his wife were naked, and they were not ashamed.
The serpent was more cunning than all the animals on the earth that God had made. The serpent said to the woman, “What is this that God told you: ‘Do not eat from the trees in the garden’?”
The woman said to the serpent, “We eat from the trees that bear fruit in the garden.
But only concerning [the fruit of] the tree in the middle of the garden, God told us not to eat from it and not to touch it, so that we would not die. That is what he said.”
The serpent said to the woman, “You will certainly not die.
Rather, God knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, [and you will become like gods], and you will know good and evil.”

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, pleasing to the eyes and to look at, and good for gaining understanding, she took its fruit and ate. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and they ate.
The eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
They heard the sound of the Lord walking in the garden toward evening, and Adam and his wife hid from the Lord among the trees of the garden.
And God called Adam and said to him, “Where are you?”
Adam said to him, “I heard your voice as you were walking about in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid.”
The Lord said to him, “Who told you that you were naked, unless you ate from this tree that I forbade you?”
Adam said, “My wife, whom you gave me to live with me, gave it to me, and I ate.”
The Lord said to the woman, “Have you done this?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”
The Lord said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, be cursed above all livestock and all wild animals of the earth. Go on your back and eat dust all the days of your life.”
“I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He shall watch your head, and you shall watch his heel.”
To the woman he said, “I will greatly increase your sorrow and your suffering. Give birth in sorrow, and your offspring [?]. Your turning will be toward your husband, and he will rule over you.”

To Adam he said, “Because you listened to your wife's voice and ate from that tree—the one tree from which I commanded you not to eat—and you ate, let the ground be cursed because of your deeds. Eat in sorrow all the days of your life.”
“It will grow thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.”
“By the sweat of your face eat your bread until you return to your earth, from which you came, because you are earth, and to earth you will return.”
And Adam named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of the living.
And God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.
The Lord said, “Look, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he learn and raise his hand and take from the tree of life and eat and live forever.”
And the Lord God sent Adam out of the garden of delight to cultivate the earth from which he had come.
He drove Adam out and settled him in front of the garden of delight. He commanded the seraphim and the cherubim, with a sword of fire that turned about, to guard the way to the tree of life.
Adam had intercourse with Eve his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. She said, “We have acquired a man through the Lord.”
She gave birth again, to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of sheep, while Cain became a cultivator of the ground.
After some days, Cain brought an offering to the Lord from the fruit of the ground.
Abel also did so and brought some of the firstborn of his sheep and some of their fattest. The Lord looked favorably on Abel and on his sacrifice and his offering.
But he did not look upon Cain or his offering. This greatly distressed Cain, and he fell on his face.
The Lord said to Cain, “Why are you sorrowful, and why has your face fallen?”
“You have not brought it in righteousness, and you should rightly bring it to me in righteousness. You have sinned; now be still. His turning will be toward you, and you will rule over him.”
Cain said to his brother Abel, “Come, let us go and walk about in the field.” While they were out in the countryside, Cain rose against his brother Abel and killed him.
And God said to Cain, “Where is Abel your brother?” And he said to him, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
The Lord said to him, “What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood has reached me from the ground.”
“And now let the ground be cursed, which opened to drink your brother's blood from your hand.”
“For you will cultivate it, but it will no longer give you its strength. Be trembling and terrified upon the earth.”
Cain said to the Lord, “Is my sin too great to be forgiven me?”
But if you drive me from the land, I will hide myself from your presence and be trembling and terrified on the earth, and everyone who finds me will kill me.

And God said to him (to Cain, “Every murderer stood likewise.” And Cain said, “I will be punished for what I have done, and I will be killed as I killed.” And the Lord said to him), “Not so. (But) everyone (who kills after you will be killed just as he killed, while you will be punished sevenfold for one) [who kills Cain will suffer sevenfold vengeance].” And the Lord placed a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.
And Cain went out from God's presence and lived in the land named Nod. (Adam remained in the land of Eden, but Cain went and settled) to the east of Eden.
And Cain had sexual relations with his wife, and she conceived and bore him Enoch. Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.
And Enoch fathered [Gaidad], and [Gaidad] fathered Mahalalel, and Mahalalel fathered Methuselah, and Methuselah fathered Lamech.
And Lamech married two women. The name of one was Zillah, and the name of the other was Adah.
And she bore Jabal, and he became the father of all who live in [enclosures as herders of] livestock.
And his brother's name was [Jubal], and he became the father of all who play pipes and perform music.
And Zillah bore [Tubal]-cain, and he worked in bronze and iron. (And [Tubal]-cain loved wealth.) [His sister's name was Naamah.]

And Lamech said to his wives, Adah and Zillah, “Listen, wives of Lamech, and pay attention to what I tell you, for I killed a man (in my forgetfulness) [for my wound], and a young man (with my blow) [for my injury].
For Cain was punished sevenfold for one, but Lamech will be punished seventy-sevenfold.”

And Adam had intercourse with Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore him a son. He named him Seth and said, “Look, now God has provided me with another offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.”
And Seth also fathered a son and named him Enosh. Then he began to call upon the name of God.
And this is the book recording Adam's ancestry. On the day when God created him, he made Adam (in the image and) in the likeness of God.
And he created them male and female. Then God blessed them and named them Adam (and Eve) on the day when he created them.
And Adam lived 230 years and fathered a son in his own image and likeness, and named him Seth.
And Adam lived 700 years after fathering Seth, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Adam's life were 930 years, and he died.
And Seth lived 205 years and fathered Enosh.
And after fathering Enosh, Seth lived 707 years and fathered sons and daughters.
And the whole span of Seth’s life was 912 years, and he died.
And Enosh lived 190 years and fathered Cainan.
And after fathering Cainan, Enosh lived 715 years and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enosh's life were 905 years, and he died.
And Cainan lived 170 years and fathered Mahalalel.
And after fathering Mahalalel, Cainan lived 740 years and fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Cainan's life were 910 years, and he died.
And Mahalalel lived 165 years and fathered Jared.
And Mahalalel lived 730 years after fathering Jared, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mahalalel's life were 6,095 years, and he died.
And Jared lived 162 years and fathered Enoch.
Jared lived 800 years after he fathered Enoch, and he had sons and daughters.
Jared's whole lifespan was 962 years, and he died.
Enoch lived 165 years and fathered Methuselah.
[Enoch pleased God.] Enoch lived 200 years after he fathered Methuselah, and he had sons and daughters.
And the whole span of Enoch’s life was 365 years.
Enoch pleased God and was taken away, because God took him (into paradise).
Methuselah lived 187 years and fathered Lamech.
Methuselah lived 782 years after he fathered Lamech, and he had sons and daughters.
All the days of Methuselah were 969 years, and he died.
Lamech lived 182 years, and a son was born to him.
He named him Noah, for he said, “This one will comfort me in my work and the toil of my hands, and concerning the ground that the Lord has cursed.”
Lamech lived 595 years after he fathered Noah, and he had sons and daughters.
Lamech's whole lifespan was 707 years, and he died.
Noah was 500 years old, and he fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And [it happened] when people began to multiply on the earth, and (sons and) daughters were born to them.
When the sons of God saw that the daughters of human beings were beautiful, they took wives from among them, choosing those they loved.
Then the Lord said, “My spirit will not dwell in these people forever, because they are flesh. But their lifespan shall be 120 years.”
In those days there were giants on the earth, because the sons of God went in to the daughters of human beings, and they bore giants to them, [men of renown from the creation of the world].
When the Lord saw that people's wickedness had become great on the earth, and that the inclinations of their thoughts and hearts were evil at all times,
the Lord regretted that he had made human beings [on the earth, and he pondered it].

God (the Lord) said, “I will wipe the human beings whom I created from the face of the earth, from humans to animals, the birds of the sky, and everything that moves, because I regret having created them.”
But Noah found mercy and favor before the Lord.
[This is the account of Noah: he was a righteous man and blameless] in his generation, and he pleased God.
He fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth became corrupt before God and was filled with violence.
God saw that the earth was corrupt and that all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
The Lord, his God, said to Noah, “The time for humanity has come before me, because the earth is filled with violence because of them. Look, I will wipe them out, and the earth as well.
Make yourself an ark of squared wood. This is how you shall make the ark: coat it with pitch, both inside and outside.
This is how you shall make the ark: 300 cubits long, [50] cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Make the ark narrow toward the top. When you approach its completion, with one cubit remaining to finish it, make its door there in its side. Make decks for it; make a second and a third level.”
And look, I am bringing floodwaters upon the earth, and I will wipe out all flesh that has the breath of life on the earth and is under heaven. All flesh will die.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter, you and your wife and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.
And from every kind of livestock, from everything that moves, from every kind of wild animal, and from all flesh, you shall bring them to you and bring them in with you, male and female.
As for you, take for yourself some of every kind of food that is eaten, and gather it to you. It will be food for you and food for them.
Noah did just as God, his God, commanded him; that is what he did.
And God said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and your whole household, for I have found you righteous before me in this generation.
Bring with you seven of each kind of clean animal, male and female, and two of each kind of unclean animal, male and female.
Of the clean birds of the sky, take seven of each kind, male and female, and of the unclean birds of the sky, two of each kind, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the earth.
For in seven more days I will bring rain upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out everything that moves upon the earth.”
And Noah did everything that God, his God, commanded him.
At that time Noah was seven hundred years old, and the flood came upon the whole earth.
And Noah and his wife [and his sons] and his sons’ wives with him entered the ark because of the floodwaters.
And from the clean birds and those that were not clean, from the clean livestock and those that were not clean, and from everything that moves upon the earth,
they entered the ark with Noah two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
And after seven days, the floodwaters came upon the earth.
In the seven hundred and first year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the twelfth day of the lunar month, on that day all the depths burst open and the floodgates of heaven were opened.
And rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that day Noah, his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, his wife, and his sons’ wives with him entered the ark.
And the wild animals according to their kinds, all the livestock according to their kinds, everything that moves, and all the birds according to their kinds entered the ark,
coming to Noah two by two from all flesh.
They entered as the Lord God had commanded, and God closed the ark from the outside.
And the flood was upon the earth for forty days and forty nights. The water filled the earth, and God lifted up the ark, and it rose above the earth.
The water grew very strong over the earth and increased, and the ark floated on the water.
The water increased exceedingly over the earth and covered all the high mountains under the sky.
The water rose fifteen [cubits] above them.
And all flesh and everything that moves upon the earth died, and every human being.
Everything that had breath and everything that was on dry land died.

Everything that moved on the face of the earth was wiped out, from human beings to animals, creeping creatures, and birds of the sky. They were wiped out from the earth. Only Noah remained, along with those who were with him in the ark.
And the water remained high above the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Noah, all the wild animals, all the livestock, and everything that was with him in the ark. God brought a wind over the earth, and the water subsided.
And the springs of the deep were closed, and the floodgates of heaven were shut, and the rain from heaven stopped.
The water began to diminish and recede from the earth, and after 150 days the water had decreased.
The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat in the seventh month, on the twelfth day of darkness.
The water continued to decrease and drain away until the tenth month. When the eleventh month came, on the first day of the new moon, the mountain peaks became visible.
After forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.
He sent out the raven to see whether the water had drained away from the surface of the earth. It went away and did not return until the water had disappeared from the earth.
After it, he sent out the dove to see whether the water had receded from the face of the earth.

She found nowhere to rest her feet and returned to him in the ark, because water still covered the whole surface of the earth. He stretched out his hand, took her, and brought her into the ark with him.
After waiting seven days, he again sent the dove out over the earth (to see).
The dove returned to him toward evening, with an olive leaf in its mouth, and Noah knew that the water had receded from the earth.
After waiting another seven days, he sent out the dove, and she did not return to him again.

In the seven hundred and first year of Noah’s life, on the first day of the new moon of the [first] month, the water had disappeared from the earth. Noah uncovered the roof of the ark that he had made and saw that the water had disappeared from the surface of the earth.
In the second month, on the twelfth day, the earth was dry.
God spoke to Noah, saying:
“Come out of the ark, you and your wife, your sons and your sons’ wives.
Bring out with you everything that is with you, every creature of flesh, from birds to livestock, and everything that moves on the earth. Be fruitful and multiply on the earth.”
Noah came out, with his wife, his sons, and his sons’ wives.
All the wild animals, livestock, birds, and everything that moves on the earth came out of the ark according to their kinds.
Noah built an altar to God. He took from the livestock and from everything that was clean and offered a sacrifice on his altar.

God smelled the pleasing fragrance, and God said, “I have resolved not to curse the earth again because of human conduct, for evil is always established in human hearts from their youth. Nor will I again destroy every living creature of flesh as I have done.
Throughout all the days of the earth, sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will not cease.”
God blessed Noah and his sons [and said to them], “Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and rule over it.
All the wild animals, the birds of the sky, everything that moves on the earth, and the fish of the sea will fear you and tremble before you. I have given them into your hands.
Every living thing that moves shall be yours for food. Just as I gave you the green plants, I have given you everything.
But you must not eat flesh containing the blood of its life.
For your own lifeblood I will demand an accounting. I will demand it from every wild animal and from the hand of every person and his brother; I will demand an accounting for every human life.
Whoever sheds human blood shall have his own blood shed in return for that blood, because I made humankind in the image of God.
But you, be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and increase upon it.”
God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying:
“Look, I give a covenant with you (on the earth), with you and your descendants after you.
With every living creature that is with you—the birds, the animals, and all the wild animals of the earth that are with you, which came out of the ark.
I establish my covenant with you: never again will all living creatures die by floodwaters, and never again will floodwaters be brought to destroy the whole earth.”
God said to Noah, “This is the sign of my covenant that I give you, between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all generations forever.
I will set my bow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of my covenant between me and the whole earth.
When I darken the clouds over the earth, my rainbow will appear in the clouds.
Then I will remember my covenant that is between you and me and every living creature among all flesh. Never again will floodwaters be brought for me to wipe out all living creatures.
My rainbow will appear in the clouds, and I will see it and remember my everlasting covenant between God and every creature on earth that has the breath of life.”
God said to Noah, “This is the [sign of] my covenant that I establish between me and you.”
These are Noah’s sons who came out of the ark: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were Noah’s sons, who spread throughout the whole earth.
After the flood, Noah began to cultivate the ground and planted a vineyard.
He drank from it, became drunk, and undressed inside his house.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw that his father was naked (and laughed). He went out and told his two brothers outside.
Shem and Japheth took a garment and placed it on both their backs. They walked backward and covered their father’s nakedness. They turned their faces away and did not see their father’s nakedness.
When Noah sobered up from his wine, he learned everything his younger son had done to him.
Noah said, “Cursed be Canaan! Let him be a servant and a slave to his brothers.”
He said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant.
May God enlarge Japheth’s territory, and may he dwell in Shem’s house, and let Canaan be his servant.”
Noah lived for 350 years after the flood.
All the days of Noah’s life were 59 years, and he died.
This is the genealogy of Noah’s sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Children were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Elishah, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
From these the islands of the nations were divided, each in its own land, according to their languages, their clans, and their nations.
The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush fathered Nimrod, who became mighty on the earth.
He was a hunter before the Lord. That is why people say, “Like Nimrod, a mighty man who was a hunter before the Lord.”
The beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, [Erech], Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
Asshur went out from that land and built Nineveh and Rehoboth, a great city.
Mizraim fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim;
the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorim.
Canaan fathered Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth;
the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites;
the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.
And the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. After this, the Canaanites scattered.
The territory of Canaan extended from Sidon to Gerar and Gaza, reaching Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Sela.
These were the sons of Ham, according to their families, their languages, their lands, and their nations.
Children were also born to Shem, the father of all the descendants of Eber and the brother of Japheth the elder.
The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber. The name of one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah;
Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah;
Obal, Abimael, Sheba, and Ophir;
Havilah and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Their settlements extended from Mesha to Sephar, reaching the mountain in the east.
These were the sons of Shem, according to their families and tribes, the languages of their lands, and their clans.
These were the tribes of Noah’s sons, according to their families. From these came those who spread out after the flood.
The whole world had one language and one form of speech.
When they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
They said to one another, “Come, let us mold bricks and bake them in fire.” Their bricks served as stone, and pitch served as their mortar.
They said, “Come, let us build a city and a tower whose top reaches into heaven, and let us make a name for ourselves, so that we are not scattered over the whole face of the earth.”
The Lord came down to look into their city and to see the tower that human beings had built.
God said, “Look, they are all one people and have one language, and this is what they have begun to do. Now they will not stop doing what they have planned.”
“Come, let us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another's speech.”
The Lord scattered them over the face of the whole earth, and they then stopped building that city and that tower.

For this reason its name was called Scattered, because there he scattered the speech of everyone [?]. The Lord scattered their speech, and there the Lord scattered the nations over the face of the whole earth.
This is the genealogy of Shem. He was one hundred years old when he fathered Arphaxad, in the second year after the flood.
After fathering Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 [years], had sons and daughters, and died.
Arphaxad lived 135 years and fathered Cainan.

After fathering Cainan, Arphaxad lived 430 years and had sons and daughters, and he died. Cainan lived 130 years and fathered Shelah. After fathering Shelah, Cainan lived 430 years and had sons and daughters, and he died.
Shelah lived 130 years and fathered Eber.
After fathering Eber, he lived [3]30 years, had sons and daughters, and died.
Eber lived 134 years and fathered Peleg.
After fathering Peleg, Eber lived 270 years and had sons and daughters, and he died.
Peleg lived 130 years and fathered Reu.
After fathering Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and had sons and daughters, and he died.
Reu lived 132 years and fathered Serug.
After fathering Serug, Reu lived 207 years and had sons and daughters, and he died.
Serug lived 135 years and fathered Nahor.
[After fathering Nahor, Serug] lived 200 [years], had sons and daughters, and died.
Nahor lived 79 years and fathered Terah.
After fathering Terah, Nahor lived 129 years and had sons and daughters, and he died.
Terah lived 70 years and fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Haran fathered Lot.
Haran died in the presence of his father Terah, in the land where he was born, in the land of the Chaldeans.
Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarai, and Nahor’s wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, who was the father of Milcah and Iscah.
Sarai was barren and did not bear children.

Terah took Abram his son, Lot the son of Haran, his brother’s son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram. He brought them out of the land of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. When they reached Haran, they settled there.
All Terah’s days in Haran amounted to 205 years, and Terah died in Haran.
The Lord said to Abram, “Leave your land, your relatives, and your father’s household, and go to the land that I will show you.
I will make you a great nation, bless you, and make your name great, and you will be blessed.
I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed because of you.
Abram went as the Lord had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
Abram took Sarai his wife, Lot his brother’s son, and all the possessions they had acquired in Haran. They set out and went to the land of Canaan.
Abram traveled through that land as far as Shechem, to the tall tree. The Canaanites were living in that land at that time.
The Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I will give this land to your descendants.” Abram built an altar there to the Lord, who had appeared to him.

He moved from there to the region of Bethel toward the east and pitched a tent there, in Bethel toward the sea, toward the east [?]. He stayed there, built an altar there to the Lord, and called on his name.
Abram arose, went on, and moved into the wilderness to stay there.
For the famine in the country was severe. Abram went down to Egypt to stay there, because the famine in the country was severe.
When Abram was close to entering Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “I know that you are a woman with a beautiful face.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, “She is his wife,” and they will kill me, but they will keep you alive.
So say, ‘I am his sister,’ so that they will treat me well because of you, and my life will be spared on your account.”
When Abram arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians saw that his wife was very beautiful.
Pharaoh’s messengers saw her, took her to Pharaoh, and brought her into his house.
They treated Abram well because of her, and he acquired sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, male slaves, female slaves, and mules.
The Lord afflicted Pharaoh and his household with great and terrible suffering because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
Pharaoh summoned Abram and said to him, “What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?
Why did you tell me, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her to be my wife? Now here she is before you. Take her and go.”
Pharaoh ordered men to send Abram away, along with his wife and all their possessions, and Lot with him, into the plains.
Abram went up from Egypt to the south, with his wife, all his possessions, and Lot with him.
Abram was greatly blessed and very rich in livestock, gold, and silver.
He returned from where he had set out, into the plain, to Bethel, to the place where his tent had been before, between Bethel and Ai.
He came to the place where he had previously built an altar, and there Abram called on the name of the Lord.
Lot, who went with Abram, also acquired sheep, cattle, and livestock.
The land could not support them living together.
There was a quarrel between Lot’s herdsmen and Abram’s herdsmen. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in that land.
Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no quarrel between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen, for we are brothers.
Look, the whole land is before you. Separate yourself from me. If you go to the right, I will go to the left; if you go to the left, I will go to the right.”
Lot lifted his eyes and saw all the plains of the Jordan. The whole land was well watered, before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. It was like the garden of the Lord and like the land of Egypt.
Lot chose all the plains of the Jordan for himself, and Lot moved away from the east. They separated from one another.
Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived among the cities and settled in Sodom.
But the people of Sodom were wicked and very sinful before the Lord.
After Lot had separated from him, the Lord said to Abram, “Look up with your eyes and see, from this place where you are, toward the north, south, east, and west.
For I will give all this land that you see to you and to your descendants forever.
I will make your descendants like the sand of the sea. If anyone can count the sand of the sea, they will also count your descendants.
Get up and walk through that land, through its length and breadth, for I will give it to you.”
Abram moved to the tree in Hebron, and there he built an altar to the Lord.
This happened during the reign of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of the nations.
They fought against Balak king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
All these joined together in the Valley of Salt, which is the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they were subject to Chedorlaomer (and the kings who were with him), but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came and killed the giants in Ashtaroth, the Karnaim, the mighty people with them, the Emim, and the city of Shaveh.
And the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as [?] and Paran, which is in the wilderness.
Turning back, they came to the pit of [?], which is Kadesh, and killed all the messengers of Amalek, the Amorites, and those living in Astana.
The king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Balak, which is Zoar, went out and engaged in battle in the Valley of Salt
with Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of the nations, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar: these four kings against those five.
That Valley of Salt was entirely full of pits. The king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah were defeated, and they killed them there. Those who were defeated fled into the mountains.
They took the horses of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their provisions, and went away.
They also took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, and their possessions, and went in. Their dwelling was in Sodom.
Some of those who escaped arrived and told Abram, while they were gathered together by the tree near the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and Aner, who were close to Abram.
When he heard that Lot, his brother’s son, had been taken captive, he counted all his own men, the men of his household. There were 318, and he pursued them and followed them as far as Dan.
He reached them at night with his servants, killed them, and pursued them as far as Hobah, which is north of Damascus.
He took their mules, and also took Lot, his brother’s son, their goods, the women, and the people.
The king of Sodom came out and met him after he returned from killing Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, in the Valley of Shaveh, which is the royal wilderness.
Melchizedek brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High, and he was king of Salem.
He blessed Abram and said to him, “Blessed is Abram by God Most High, who created heaven and earth.
“And blessed be God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hands.” And he gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, and keep the horses for yourself.”
Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I raise my hand to the Lord, God Most High, who made heaven and earth,
that not even a thread or a sandal strap will be taken from your possessions, so that you cannot say, ‘I made Abram rich.’
Except for what my men have eaten and the share of the men who came with me—Eshcol, Aner, and Mamre. Let these men take their share.”
After this, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, and he said to him, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I will strengthen you, and your reward with me is very great.”
Abram said to him, “Lord, what will you give me? Look, I will die without a child, and the son of Masek of Damascus, who is called Iyaubr [?], who comes from my family, will inherit from me.”
Abram said, “Since you have given me no offspring, someone born in my family will inherit from me.”
Then the word of the Lord came, saying, “This man will not be your heir. Another will come from you, and he will be your heir.”
He brought him outside and said to him, “Look up into the sky and count the stars, if you can count them.” And he said to him, “So will your offspring be.”
Abram believed the Lord, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
He said to him, “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.”
He said to him, “Lord, how will I know that I will possess it?”
He said to him, “Take for yourself a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old goat, a three-year-old sheep, a turtledove, and a pigeon.
Take all these as well and cut them down the middle, but do not cut the birds.”
Those birds came down upon their kin that had been cut apart, and Abram sat beside them.
As the sun was setting, a trance came upon Abram, and a great, terrifying darkness came over him.
They said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs. They will enslave them, afflict them, and oppress them for four hundred years.”
“But I will judge the nation that afflicts them, and afterward they will come out here with many possessions.”
“But you will go and be gathered to your ancestors at a good old age.”
“In the fourth generation they will return here, because the sins of the Amorites have not yet reached their full measure.”
When the time came for the sun to set, a flame appeared, and fire appeared, and a smoking furnace appeared and passed between what he had cut apart.
On that day the Lord confirmed to Abram what he had promised him, saying, “To your descendants I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates.”
That of the Kenites, that of the Kenizzites, and that of the Kadmonites;
and that of the Hittites, that of the Perizzites, and that of the Rephaim;
and that of the Amorites, that of the Canaanites, that of the Girgashites, and that of the Jebusites.
Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. She had an Egyptian slave woman whose name was Hagar.

Sarai said to Abram in the land of Canaan, “Look, the Lord God has prevented me from bearing children. Go, then, and sleep with my slave woman, so that you may have children by her.” Abram listened to Sarai.
After Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years, Sarai took Hagar, her Egyptian slave woman, and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
Abram slept with Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, she stopped respecting her mistress.

Sarai said to Abram, “I am being wronged because of you. I gave my slave woman into your embrace, and when she saw that she had conceived, she stopped respecting me. May the Lord judge between me and you.”
Abram said to Sarai his wife, “Your slave woman is in your hands. Do to her as you see fit.” Sarai mistreated Hagar, and she fled from her.
The angel of the Lord found her beside a spring of water along the road in the wilderness of Shur.
The angel of the Lord said to her, “Hagar, Sarai’s slave woman, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She said to him, “I am fleeing from my mistress Sarai.”
The angel of the Lord said to her, “Return to your mistress and humble yourself under her authority.”
The angel of the Lord said to her, “I will greatly multiply your descendants, so that they cannot be counted because they are so numerous.”
The angel of the Lord said to her, “Look, you are pregnant and will give birth to a son. You shall name him Ishmael, because the Lord has heard your suffering.”
“He will be a man of the wilderness. His hands will be against everyone, and everyone’s hands will be against him. He will live in the presence of his brothers.”
Hagar called upon the name of the Lord who had spoken to her and said, “You, Lord, are the one who sees me, for I saw before me the one who appeared to me.”
For this reason she named that well “The Well of the One Who Appeared Before Me.” It is between Kadesh and Bered. (And Hagar returned.)
After this, Hagar bore a child to Abram, and Abram named the child whom Hagar bore to him Ishmael.
Abram was eighty-seven years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
Then, when Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God. Be pleasing before me and be blameless.”
“I will establish a covenant between me and you, and I will greatly multiply you.”
Abram fell on his face, and God said to him:
“Look, I will establish my covenant with you, and you will become the father of many nations.”
“Your name will no longer be Abram, but you will be called Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.”
“I will multiply you exceedingly, and I will cause nations and kings to come from you.”
“I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations, to be an everlasting law for you, so that I am God.”
“I will give your descendants this land in which you live, and all the land of Canaan, for them to rule over forever. And I will be their God.”
God said to Abraham, “You must keep my law, you and your descendants after you throughout their generations.”
“This is my ordinance, which you must keep between me and you and your descendants after you: you must circumcise every male among you.”
“You must circumcise the foreskin of your flesh, and it will be an ordinance between me and you.”
“You must circumcise a child at eight days old, every male among you throughout your generations, including those born in your household and all those you have bought with your gold.”
“My ordinance in your flesh will be my everlasting covenant.”
“Anyone whose foreskin has not been circumcised at eight days old shall be cut off from his kin, because that person has abandoned my ordinance.”
God said to Abraham, “Your wife Sarai shall no longer be called Sarai; her name shall be Sarah.”
“For I will bless her and give her children by you; nations and kings of nations will come from her.”
Abraham fell on his face and laughed, thinking in his heart, “Will I father a son when I am a hundred years old? And will Sarah give birth when she is ninety years old?”
Abraham said to God, “Then let this Ishmael live before you for me, I beg you, Lord.”

God said to Abraham, “Yes, and look, your wife Sarah will also bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac. I will establish my ordinance with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his descendants after him.”
“As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I will bless him and multiply him and increase him greatly. He will father twelve nations, and I will make him a great nation.”
“But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”
When God finished speaking, he went up from Abraham.

Abraham took his son Ishmael, everyone born in his household, every male purchased with his money, and all the men of Abraham’s household, and circumcised the foreskins of their bodies, as God had told him.
Abraham was ninety-nine years old at the time when the foreskin of his flesh was circumcised.
His son Ishmael was thirteen years old when the foreskin of his body was circumcised.
On that very day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.
All the men of his household were circumcised.
God appeared to Abraham by the tree of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent at noon.
When he lifted his eyes and looked, there were three men standing over him. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of the tent to meet them and bowed down to the ground.
He said to them, “My lords, if I have found favor in your eyes—”
“Let us bring water and wash your feet, and you can rest in the shade under the tree.”
“Let us bring bread for you to eat, and afterward you may go where you intended, since you have stopped at your servant’s home.” They said to him, “Do as you have said.”
Abraham ran to his wife Sarah in her tent and said to her, “Hurry! Knead three measures of fine flour and make flatbreads.”
Abraham ran to the cattle, took a young, good calf, and gave it to his servant, who hurried to prepare it.
He brought curds (and honey) and the calf he had prepared, and set them before them. They ate while he stood by the tree and fanned them.
They said to him, “Where is your wife Sarah?” He said to them, “There she is, in the tent.”
He said to him, “When I return, I will come to you a year from today, and Sarah will have a son.” Sarah heard this while standing at the entrance, behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were very old and advanced in years, and Sarah’s monthly periods had stopped.
Sarah laughed to herself, saying in her heart, “Can I still do this now, when my lord is also old?”
God said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh to herself, saying, (‘Can I still do this now, when my lord is also old?’ and) ‘Will I really give birth, now that I have grown old?’”
“Is anything impossible for God? At this time, when I return to you, Sarah will have a son.”
Sarah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. But he said to her, “No, you did laugh.”
Those (two) men rose from there and looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
The Lord said, “I will not hide from my servant Abraham what I am going to do.
For Abraham will become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed through him.

For I know that Abraham is to command his children and his household and have them keep the ways of God, practicing righteousness and justice, so that God may fulfill for Abraham (and for them) everything he has promised him.”
God said to him, “The outcry concerning Sodom and Gomorrah has grown great, and their sin has become very grave.
So I will go down and see whether they have acted fully in accordance with the outcry that has come to me. If not, I will know.”
When those men turned away from there, they came into Sodom (and Gomorrah), but Abraham was still standing before God.
Abraham approached and said, “Lord, do not destroy the righteous along with sinners, and do not let the righteous be treated like the sinner.
If there are fifty righteous people in the city, will you destroy them? Will you not spare the whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous people?”
Far be it from you, Lord! Do not do this, and do not kill the righteous along with the sinners. Far be it from you, who judge the whole earth! Do not carry out such a judgment.
God said to Abraham, “If I find fifty righteous people within the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole city for their sake.”
Abraham answered and said, “Now I have undertaken to speak with my Lord God, though I am earth and dust.”

“But if those righteous people are five short, will you destroy the whole city because of the five who are missing?” The Lord said to him, “If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it for their sake.”
Abraham said to him, “What if forty are found there?” The Lord said to him, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the forty.”
Abraham spoke again and said to him, “But if thirty are found there?” He said to him, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the thirty.”
Abraham said to him, “Since I have dared to speak with God, what if twenty are found there?” He said to him, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the twenty.”
Abraham said, “Allow me to speak once more, Lord. What if ten are found there?” He said to him, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten.”
When he had finished speaking with Abraham, God departed, and Abraham returned to his dwelling.
The two angels came into Sodom toward evening. Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. When he saw them, he rose and welcomed them [and bowed down to them].

He said to them, “My lords, turn aside to your servant’s house, spend the night, and wash your feet. Then you can rise early and go on your way.” They said to him, “No, we will spend the night in the square.”

(And he bowed down to them with his face to the ground.) He urged them, and they turned aside to stay with him and entered his house. He made unleavened bread for them and gave them something to drink, and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of that city surrounded their house—all their people together, young and old.
They called to Lot and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we may have our way with them.”
Lot went out to them at the doorway and shut the door behind him.
He said to them, “Far be it from you, my brothers! Do not mistreat these men.”

“Look, I have two daughters who have not known a man.” He brought them out to them and said, “Here they are. Do to them whatever pleases you. But do no violence at all to these men, who have come under the shelter of my house.”
They said to him, “Get away! You came here to stay, not to judge us. Now we will mistreat you more than those men.” They pressed hard against the man and came forward to break down the door.
Those men stretched out their hands, pulled Lot in, and brought him into the house with them [and shut the door].
They blinded the eyes of the men who were outside the door of that house, young and old. They wore themselves out searching for the door but could not find it.
They said to Lot, “Do you have a brother-in-law here, or a son-in-law, or sons and daughters? If you have any friend you know in this city, bring them out of this place.”
“For we are going to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has become great before God, and he has sent us to wipe it out.”

Lot went out to his sons-in-law, who had married his (two) daughters, and said to them, “Get up and leave this city, because God will wipe out this city.” But his sons-in-law thought he was speaking to them in jest.
At daybreak, the angels began urging Lot, saying to him, “Get up, take your two daughters and your wife, and leave, so that you too do not die because of the sins of this city.”
Those men took hold of his hand, his wife’s hands, and those of his two daughters, because the Lord had mercy on them.

When they had brought him outside, they said to him, “Escape and save your life! Do not look behind you, and do not stop anywhere in its surrounding territory. Save yourself in the mountains, so that disaster does not overtake you too.”
Lot said to them, “Please, my lords!”
“For I have found mercy in your sight, and you have shown me great mercy by keeping me alive. But I cannot escape to the mountain, lest disaster overtake me and I die.”
“Look, this city is nearby and small. Let me run there and save myself. Is it not small? [?] my life may be saved.”
He said to him, “Look, I have spared it for your sake. As you have asked, I will not overthrow the city about which you spoke to me.”
“Hurry, then, and escape there.” For this reason that town was named Zoar.
The Lord rained fire and sulfur upon Sodom and Gomorrah, from the Lord out of heaven.
He overthrew those cities and their surrounding territories, together with everyone living in the cities and the crops of their land.
Lot’s wife looked behind her and became a pillar of salt.
Early in the morning Abraham went to the place where he had stood before the Lord.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the surrounding land. As he looked, there was smoke rising from the earth like the smoke of a furnace.
When he destroyed all the towns and all the surrounding land, God remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the midst of the destruction, when God destroyed those towns in which he lived.
Lot went up from Zoar and fled to the mountain, with his two daughters, because he was afraid to live in Zoar. He lived in a cave, he and his two daughters.
The older daughter said to the younger, “Look, our father is old, and there is no man to come to us to have children, as people do throughout the earth.
Come, let us give our father wine to drink and sleep with him, so that we may preserve offspring through our father.”
They gave their father wine to drink that night. The older daughter went in and slept with her father that night, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

Afterward the older daughter said to the younger, “Look, I slept with our father yesterday. Let us give him wine to drink again, and you sleep with him tonight, so that we may preserve offspring through our father.”
They gave him wine to drink that night. The younger daughter went in and slept with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
Both of Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter bore a son and named him Moab, meaning “from my father.” He became the ancestor of the Moabites to this day.
The younger daughter also bore a son and named him Ammon, saying, “A child of my kin.” He is the ancestor of the Ammonites to this day.
Abraham set out from there and went toward the southern land. He stayed between Kadesh and Shur and lived in Gerar.
Abraham said to them about Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
God came to Abimelech that night while he was sleeping and said to him, “Look, you will die because of the woman you have taken, for she is another man’s wife.”
But Abimelech had not touched her. Abimelech said, “Will you kill a people who did not know and are righteous?
He himself told me, ‘She is my sister,’ and she also told me, ‘I am his sister.’ I did this with a pure heart and innocent hands.”
God said to him in the dream, “I also knew that you did this with a pure heart, and I held you back from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you approach her.
Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not return her, know that you will surely die, you and all who belong to you.”
Abimelech rose in the morning, called all his servants, and told them what had happened. All the people of his household were very afraid of God.
Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to me and my kingdom—a great sin! You have done to me what no one should do.”
Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see that led you to do this?”
Abraham said to him, “Because I thought, ‘Surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’
For she is my sister on my father’s side, but not on my mother’s side, and she became my wife.”
“When God brought me out of my father’s house, I said, ‘Show me this kindness: wherever we go, say, “He is my brother.”’”
Abimelech took a thousand pieces of silver, sheep, cattle, male servants, and female servants and gave them to Abraham. He also returned Sarah his wife to him.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “Look, my land is before you.”
He said to Sarah, “Look, I have given your brother a thousand pieces. Let this serve to honor you before everyone who is with you. Speak truthfully in everything.”
Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and their female servants, and they bore children.
For the Lord had completely closed the wombs of the women in Abimelech's household because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
The Lord visited Sarah, and the Lord did for her as he had said.
Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the time God had told him.
Abraham named the child whom Sarah bore him Isaac.
Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac was born to him.
Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears will rejoice with me.”
She said, “Who would have told me—to Abraham [?]—that Sarah would nurse a child whom she bore in her old age?”
The child grew and was weaned. Abraham gave a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
When Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian playing with her son Isaac,
Sarah said to Abraham, “Send this slave woman away with her son, for the slave woman's son will not inherit with my son Isaac.”
This matter distressed Abraham greatly because of his son.
God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the child or the slave woman. Listen to Sarah in everything she tells you, for your descendants will be reckoned through Isaac.
I will also make the son of that slave woman into a great nation, because he is your offspring.”

Abraham rose in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar. He put them on her shoulder, along with the child, and sent her away. She went and wandered in the wilderness toward the Well of the Oath.
When the water in her skin ran out, she left her child under a tree.
She went and sat watching him from a distance, about a bowshot away, for she said, “Let me not see my child die.” And she wept.

God heard the child's cry from the place where he was. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard your child's voice from the place where he is.
Get up, lift up your child, and hold him firmly in your hands, for I will make him into a great nation.”
God opened Hagar's eyes, and she saw a well of fresh water. She went and filled her skin with water and gave her child a drink.
God was with the child, and he grew up. He lived in that wilderness and became an archer.
Then, in the wilderness of Paran, his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech, Ahuzzath, the overseer of his herds, and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, “God is with you in everything you do.
Now swear to us by God that you will not wrong us, my offspring, or those with me. Instead, treat me and my land, in which you are living, as I treated you when you came.”
Abraham said, “Yes, I will swear.”
Abraham complained about the well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.
Abimelech said to him, “I did not know who did this. You did not tell me, and I had not heard about it until today.”
Abraham took cattle and sheep and gave them to Abimelech, and they swore an oath to each other.
Abraham set seven sheep apart by themselves.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “What are these seven sheep that you have set apart by themselves?”
Abraham said to him, “Accept these seven sheep from me, so that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well.”
For this reason they named that well the Well of the Oath, because there they swore an oath to each other.
They made a covenant at the Well of the Oath. Then Abimelech rose, along with Ahuzzath, his wedding attendant, and Phicol, the commander of his army, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a field at the Well of the Oath, and there Abraham called upon the name of the everlasting Lord.
Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines for many days.
After these days, God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said to him, “Take your son whom you love, your Isaac, and go to the high mountain. Bring him up to me and sacrifice him on one of the mountains that I will tell you about.”

Abraham rose in the morning and saddled his donkey. He took two of his servants and also his son Isaac, and chopped wood for the sacrifice. He set out and, on the third day, reached the place God had told him about.
Abraham said to the young men, “Stay here with the donkey. My son and I will go over there, and after we have worshiped, we will return to you.”
Abraham took the wood for the sacrifice and made his son Isaac carry it. He himself took the fire and the knife in his hands, and the two of them went together.
Isaac said to Abraham his father, “Father!” He said to him, “What is it, my son?” He said to him, “Here are the wood and the fire, but where is the sheep for the sacrifice?”
Abraham said to him, “God will provide himself a sheep for the sacrifice, my son.” And they went together.
They reached the place God had told him about. Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on his stomach on the altar, on top of the wood.
Abraham raised his hand to take the knife and slaughter his son.
The Lord God called to Abraham and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” He answered, “Here I am.”
He said to him, “Do not lay your hand on your son or do anything at all to him. Now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld from me your son whom you love.”
When Abraham looked, he saw a ram caught by its horns in a Sabek tree. Abraham went and took it and sacrificed it in place of his son Isaac.
Abraham named that place “The Lord Saw,” as people say today, “On the mountain the Lord saw.”
The angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time from heaven.
He said to him, “I have sworn by myself, says the Lord: Because you have done this and have not withheld from me your son whom you love,
I will surely bless you and greatly multiply your descendants, making them like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the cities of their enemies.
Through your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you obeyed my voice.”
Abraham returned to his servants, and they set out and went together to the Well of the Oath.
After these things, news was brought to Abraham, and they told him, “Milcah has borne children to your brother Nahor:
Uz, her firstborn, Buz his brother, and Kemuel, the father of the Syrians;
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel,
who fathered Rebekah. These are the children Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
His concubine Reumah bore him Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lived 127 years.
Sarah died in the city of Kiriath-arba, in the lowlands, which is Hebron in Canaan. Abraham went up to mourn Sarah and weep for her.
Abraham rose from beside her body and said to the descendants of Heth,
“I am a stranger and a foreign resident among you. Allow me to buy a burial place among you and bury my dead.”
The descendants of Heth answered Abraham, saying, “No, my lord.
Listen to us. You are a king among us, appointed by God. Bury your dead in whichever of our tombs you choose. None of us will withhold his tomb from you, preventing you from burying your dead there.”
Abraham rose and bowed before the people, the descendants of Heth.
Abraham said to them, “If you are willing to let me bury my dead, speak on my behalf to Ephron son of Zohar.
Give me his double cave, which is in his field. Give it to me for my gold, at its full price, and I will buy it from you.”
Ephron was sitting among the descendants of Heth. Ephron the Hittite spoke to Abraham in the hearing of the descendants of Heth and everyone entering the town:
“Come near me, my lord, and listen to me. I give you the field and the cave within it. Before all the people of my city, here, I have given it to you. Bury your dead.”
Abraham bowed before all the people.
He said to Ephron in everyone’s hearing, “Since you are close to me, listen to me. Accept the price of that field from me, and I will bury my dead there.”
Ephron answered Abraham and said to him,
“No, my lord, I have heard. What is this, and what are four hundred shekels between me and you? Bury your dead there, then.”
Abraham listened to Ephron, in accordance with what he had told him before the descendants of Heth. Abraham sent Ephron four hundred shekels of silver as payment, which was not [?].
Ephron’s field, its cave, and all the trees within it became his.
It became Abraham’s, and he bought it before the descendants of Heth.
After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the double cave that he had bought from Ephron.
Abraham grew old and was advanced in years, and the Lord blessed Abraham in everything.
Abraham said to his eldest son, who managed all his possessions, “Put your hand upon my hand.”
“I will make you swear by the God of heaven and earth that you will not take a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of Canaan, among whom I live.
Instead, go to my country, where I was born, and take a wife for my son Isaac from there.”
His servant said to him, “If the woman is unwilling to come with me to this country, should I take your son back to the land from which you came?”
Abraham said to his servant, “Be careful not to take my son back there.

The Lord, the God of heaven and earth, who brought me out of my fathers’ household and out of the land where I was born, who swore to me and said, ‘I will give this land to you and to your descendants,’ will send his angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.”
“But if the woman is unwilling to come with you to this land, you are free from the oath. Only take care not to bring my son back there.”
The servant placed his hand on the hand of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.
The servant took ten camels from his master’s camels and took with him all kinds of his master’s fine things. He set out and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
He made his camels rest outside the city, beside the well of water, toward evening, at the time when the women who drew water came out.
And he said, “My Lord, God of Abraham,
here I stand beside the well of water, and the daughters of the people of the town are coming out to draw water.”

“Let it be the virgin to whom I say, ‘Lower your jar so that I may drink water,’ and who says to me, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels water until they have had enough.’ Let her be the one you have prepared for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown mercy to my master Abraham.”

Before he had finished speaking this way in his heart, there was Rebekah coming out. She was born to Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, and she was carrying a jar on her shoulder.
The young woman was very beautiful. She was a virgin and had never known a man. She went down into the well and drew water, and when she came up,
the man ran and said to her, “Give me a little water to drink from your jar.”
She said to him, “Drink, my lord.” She quickly lowered the jar she carried on her shoulder and gave him a drink until he had had enough.
Then she said to him, “I will also draw water for your camels, so that they may all drink.”
She quickly emptied her jar into the drinking trough, then ran and drew water for all his camels.
The man watched her [?] and remained silent to see whether the Lord would make his journey successful or not.
After his camels had had enough to drink, the man took gold earrings, each weighing a shekel, and bracelets for her hands, each weighing ten shekels.
He asked her, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me whether there is a place for us to stay in your father’s house.”
She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, who was born to Nahor.
We have grass and feed, and also a place for your camels to stay.”
The man was amazed and bowed down to the Lord.

He said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withdrawn his righteousness and faithfulness from my master. He has guided me on my way to the house of the brother of my master Abraham.”
The young woman went and told her mother’s household about this.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and Laban ran out to that man at the well.
When he saw his sister Rebekah’s earrings and bracelets, and she said, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man, who was standing beside the well.
He said to him, “Come, enter! Blessed be the Lord! Why are you standing outside? Look, we have prepared lodging and a shelter for your camels.”
The man entered and lodged his camels. They brought him straw and feed for his camels, and they brought him water for his feet and for the men who were with him.
They brought him bread to eat, but he said to them, “I will not eat until I have said what I have to say.” They said to him, “Speak.”
He said to them, “I am Abraham’s servant.
The Lord has greatly blessed my master and made him great. He has given him cattle and sheep, gold and silver, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
Sarah, the wife of my master Abraham, bore him one son in his old age, and he has given him everything he has.
My master made me swear an oath and said to me, ‘Do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of Canaan, among whom I live.
Instead, go to my father’s house and to my clan, and take a wife for my son from there.’
I said to my master, ‘Perhaps the woman will not be willing to come with me.’

My master said to me, “The Lord God, whom I have pleased, will send his angel ahead of you and make your journey successful. You will take a wife for my son from there, (and if not [?]) from my clan, and [?] in my father’s household.”
Then you will be free from my oath; and if they refuse to give her to you, you are free from the oath.
When I came here to the well, I said, “Lord, God of my master Abraham, if you have guided me today on this journey I am making—
here I stand beside the well of water, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water. Let the virgin to whom I say, ‘Please give me a little water to drink from your jar,’

and who says to me, ‘Drink, and I will also draw water for your camels,’ be the woman you have prepared for your servant Isaac, Lord. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master Abraham.”
Before I had finished thinking this in my heart, Rebekah came out carrying her jar. She went down into the well and drew water, and I said to her, “Give me a drink.”
She quickly lowered her jar and said, “Drink, and I will also give your camels water.”

I questioned her and said, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me.” She said to me, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.” I adorned her with earrings and put bracelets on her hands.
And when she [?] me, I bowed down to the Lord and praised the God of Abraham, who had guided me on the right path to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
If you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; otherwise I will turn either to the right or to the left.
Bethuel and Laban answered him, saying, “This matter has come from the Lord, and we cannot answer either good or bad.”
“Here is Rebekah. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, as the Lord has said.”
When he heard this, he bowed down to the ground.
The man brought out gold and silver jewelry and fine clothes and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave gifts to her brother and her mother.
Then he and those with him ate and drank and spent the night. They rose in the morning, and he said, “Send me away so that I may go to my master.”
Her brother and her mother said, “Let our daughter stay with us for ten days, and then she may go.”
He said to them, “Do not hold me back, since the Lord has made my journey successful. Send me away so that I may go to my master.”
They said to him, “Let us call Rebekah and hear from her own mouth.”
They called Rebekah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” She said, “I will go.”
They sent Rebekah away with her belongings, and they also sent Abraham’s son away with those who were with him.

They blessed their sister Rebekah and said to her, “You are our sister. May you become tens of thousands, and tens of thousands of tens of thousands, and may your descendants possess the cities of their enemies.”
Rebekah and her nurse (Deborah) rose, mounted their camels, and went with the man. The man took charge of Rebekah, and they departed.
Isaac was traveling in the wilderness toward the well, and they were living in the land to the south.
Isaac went out to walk in the wilderness toward evening. When he looked, he saw camels coming.
When Rebekah looked, she saw Isaac and got down from her camel.
She asked the young man, “Who is this man walking in the wilderness to meet us?” The man said to her, “This is my master.” She took a veil and covered her face.
He told Isaac, his son, everything he had done.
Isaac entered his mother’s house, and then he took Rebekah, and she became his wife. He loved her, and Isaac’s grief over his mother was soothed.
Abraham married again, taking a wife whose name was Keturah.
And she bore sons named Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Jokshan fathered Sheba, Teman, and Dedan. Dedan fathered Raguel, Nababzo, Ezraam, and Leummim.
The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.
Abraham gave all his possessions to his son Isaac.
Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and, while he was still alive, sent them away from his son Isaac toward the east.
This was Abraham’s lifespan: his years were one hundred and seventy-five years.
Abraham died when he was very old, at a good old age, having completed his days, and he was gathered to his people.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave in the field of Ephron, son of Zohar the Hittite, opposite Mamre,
the field and cave that Abraham had bought from the Hittites. There they buried Abraham and his wife Sarah.
After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac, and Isaac lived near the Well of Vision.
This is the genealogy of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar, Sarah’s servant, bore to him.
These are the names of Ishmael’s sons: his firstborn Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam;
Mishma, Dumah, and Massa;
Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are Ishmael’s sons, and these are their names according to their towns and their settlements: twelve princes of their peoples.
The years of Ishmael’s life were 137 years. He died in old age and was buried among his relatives.
He lived alone from Havilah to Shur, which is in Egypt, and reached as far as Assyria. He lived opposite all his brothers.
This is the account of the descendants of Isaac, Abraham’s son.
Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah as his wife. She was the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian from Mesopotamia and the sister of Laban the Syrian.
Isaac prayed to the Lord on behalf of his wife Rebekah because she was barren. The Lord heard him, and his wife Rebekah conceived.
Her children struggled together in her womb, and she said, “If this is how it is for me, why is this happening to me?” She went to inquire of the Lord God.
The Lord God said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will come out of your womb. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.”
The time for her to give birth was completed, and there were two children in her womb.
Her firstborn son came out red all over like a rose blossom and hairy, and she named him Esau.
After him his brother came out, holding Esau’s heel with his hand, and she named him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah gave birth to them (Esau and Jacob).
They grew up and became young men. Esau became a hunter, a man of the fields, while Jacob had an unpleasant appearance and stayed at home.
Isaac loved his son Esau because he ate what Esau hunted, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
She cooked a stew for her son Jacob, and Esau came in from the fields.
