as soon as he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die, and we will bring the gray hair of your servant, our father, down to the grave in anguish.”

For your servant pledged himself to his father for this child, saying to him, “If I do not bring him back to you and set him before you, let me bear the guilt before you, Father, all the days of my life.”
Now let me be your servant in place of this child and remain with you, my lord, and let the child go with his brothers.
For how can I go to our father without this child with us? I must not see the disaster that would befall our father.

Joseph could no longer restrain himself while everyone stood before him. Joseph said, “Send everyone away from me.” They sent everyone out from his presence, and no one else remained there with Joseph when he made himself known to his brothers.
He cried out and wept, and all Egypt heard him, and it was heard in Pharaoh’s household too.
He said to them, “I am Joseph, your brother. Is our father still alive?” They could not answer him, because they were terrified.
And Joseph said to his brothers, “Come close to me.” And they came close to him. And Joseph said to them, “I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold into the land of Egypt.”
Now let there be no fear in your eyes because you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to preserve life.
For two years of famine have now passed over the land, and there are still five years in which no one will plow.
“And God sent me ahead of you so that you might live and survive on the earth, and so that I might provide for you.”
So it was not you who sent me, but God. He made me a son to Pharaoh, lord over all [his household and ruler over all] Egypt.
Now go quickly and tell my father, “This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord over the whole land of Egypt. Come down quickly, then, and do not remain there.”
“You will live in the land of Goshen in Arabia and be near me—you, your children, your sheep, your cattle, and everything you have.”
“I will provide for you there, because there are still five years of famine, so that neither you nor anything you own will perish.”
You see with your own eyes, and my brother Benjamin has seen with his own eyes, that it is I myself speaking to you with my own mouth.
Tell my father about all my honor in the land of Egypt and everything you have seen, and hurry to bring my father here.
He put his arms around his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept over him, and Benjamin too wept on his neck.
He kissed them all and wept over them. After this, his brothers spoke to him.
And the news was heard in Pharaoh’s house: “Joseph’s brothers have come.” And Pharaoh and all his people rejoiced.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Fill your containers and go to the land of Canaan.’”
“Take your father and all your possessions and come to me. I will give you a share of all Egypt’s abundance, and you will eat the richest produce of the land.”
As for you, give your brothers this command: Let them take carts from the land of Egypt for their children and their wives, and let them take your father and bring him.
“Let them not be concerned about their belongings or what their eyes behold, for all the bounty of Egypt belongs to them.”
The sons of Israel did just as they had been told. Joseph gave them carts as Pharaoh, king of Egypt, had commanded, and gave them provisions for the journey.
He gave each of them two sets of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred dinars and five changes of clothes.
And likewise for his father: he sent ten donkeys carrying some of all the bounty of Egypt, and ten mules carrying provisions for his father’s journey.
He sent his brothers away and said to them, “Do not quarrel on the journey.”
They left the land of Egypt and reached the land of Canaan, where their father was.
They brought him the news and said to him, “Your son Joseph is alive, and he is ruler over the whole land of Egypt.” His heart was stunned, and he did not believe them.
They told him everything Joseph had said to them and everything he had discussed with them. When he saw the carts Joseph had sent, the heart and spirit of Jacob their father revived.
Jacob said, “This is a great thing for me, if my son Joseph is still alive! I will go and see him before I die.”
Israel set out with all his possessions, and they reached Beersheba. There he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
The God of Israel spoke to him in a dream at night, saying, “Jacob, Jacob!” He replied, “What is it?”
He said to him, “I am the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you a great nation there.
I will go down with you into the land of Egypt, and I will always remain with you. Joseph will close your eyes.”
Jacob set out from Beersheba. Jacob’s sons carried Israel their father, with their possessions and their wives, and loaded them into the carts Joseph had sent to bring them.
They took their possessions and all the livestock they had acquired in the land of Canaan. Jacob entered the land of Egypt, and all his descendants were with him:
his sons and his sons’ sons, his daughters and his daughters’ daughters were with him.
These are the names of the sons of Israel who entered the land of Egypt: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
The sons of Reuben were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, whose mother was a Canaanite woman.
The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. These were the sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Issachar were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
The sons of Zebulun were Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These were the children of Leah whom she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, together with his daughter Dinah. His sons and daughters numbered thirty-three persons in all.
The sons of Gad were Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
The sons of Asher were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and Serah was their sister. These were the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the descendants of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah. She bore them to Jacob: sixteen people.
And the sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife, were Joseph and Benjamin.

And children were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt: Manasseh and Ephraim. And the son of Manasseh whom his Syrian concubine bore him was [Machir, and Machir fathered Gilead]. And the sons of Ephraim, Manasseh’s brother, were [Shuthelah and Tahan, and the son of Shuthelah was Eden].
The sons of Benjamin were Bela, Becher, and Ashbel. These were the sons of Bela: Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, and Muppim. Gera fathered Ard.
These are the descendants of Rachel whom she bore to Jacob: eighteen people.
The son of Dan: Asa.
The sons of Naphtali: Asiel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These are the descendants of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel. She bore these to Jacob, and all the people whom Bilhah bore numbered seven.
All the people who entered the land of Egypt with Jacob, excluding the wives, numbered sixty-six.
The descendants of Joseph who were born to him in the land of Egypt numbered seven. All the people who entered the land of Egypt with Jacob numbered seventy-five.
He sent Judah into the city to Joseph, so that Joseph would meet him in the land of Rameses, whose name is Qateroas.
Joseph prepared his chariots and went to meet his father Jacob in the city of Heroonpolis. When he met him, he embraced him around the neck and wept bitterly.
Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face and you are alive.”
Joseph said to his brothers, “I will go and tell Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘My brothers and my father's household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
The men are livestock herders, and they have brought all their possessions and their cattle.’
If Pharaoh calls you and asks you, ‘What is your occupation?’

tell him, ‘We, your servants, have been livestock herders from our youth until now, and our fathers were the same,’ so that you may live in the land of Goshen, which is in Arabia, because the Egyptians detest all shepherds.”
Joseph came and told Pharaoh, saying, “My father and my brothers, their livestock, and all their possessions have come from the land of Canaan. They have now arrived in the land of Goshen.”
Joseph took five men from among his brothers and brought them with him to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Joseph's brothers, “What is your occupation?” They said to Pharaoh, “We, your servants, are shepherds, both we and our fathers.”

They said to Pharaoh, “Let us live in the land to which we have come, because there is no pasture for your servants' livestock, and the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now let your servants live in the land of Goshen.”
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since your father and your brothers have come to you,

the land of Egypt is before you. Let your father and your brothers live in the best part of it. If you know that there are capable men among them, appoint them as overseers of the herders of my livestock.”
Joseph brought his father and presented him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How long have you lived?”

Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The years of my life that I have lived are one hundred and thirty. The days and years of my life have been few and miserable, and they have been as nothing compared with the days that my fathers lived.”
After Jacob blessed Pharaoh, he left his presence.
Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best part of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded for them.
Joseph measured out wheat as food for his father, his brothers, and his father's entire household. He measured out a ration of wheat for each person.
There was no wheat anywhere in the land of Egypt, because the famine was very severe. The lands of Egypt and Canaan were devastated by the famine.
Joseph gathered all the gold that the people of Egypt and the people of Canaan brought as payment for the grain he sold them. Joseph brought all the gold into Pharaoh's house.

All the gold in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan was exhausted. All the people of Egypt came to Joseph and said to him, “Give us food so that we do not die before you, for our gold is exhausted.”
Joseph said to them, “Bring your livestock, and I will give you grain in exchange for your livestock, if your gold has run out.”
They brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their sheep and cattle. In exchange for their donkeys, too, he supplied them with food that year.

That year ended, and they came to him in the second year and said to him, “So that we do not die or perish, our lord: our gold, our possessions, and our livestock are exhausted, and we have used them all up, my lord. Nothing remains for us before you, my lord, except our own bodies and our land.”

So that we do not die before you and our land does not become desolate, take us and buy us and our land in exchange for grain. We will become Pharaoh’s slaves, and our land will belong to him. Give us seed so that we may sow and live and not die, and so that our land does not become desolate.
Joseph bought all the Egyptians’ land and transferred all their land to Pharaoh, because the famine had overpowered them. All the land became Pharaoh’s.
All the people became his slaves, and he took possession of them from the ends of the land, along with their mountains and all the territory of Egypt, from the ends of their territory.

The only exception was the priests’ land, which Joseph did not buy, because Pharaoh gave to the priests, distributed provisions to them, and supported them. For this reason they did not sell their land.
Joseph spoke to all the people of Egypt and said to them, “Look, I have bought you and your land for Pharaoh. Take seed for yourselves and sow your land.”
“You must give Pharaoh a fifth share (portion) of the grain, and four shares will be yours, to provide seed for your land and food for yourselves and all your people.”
They said to him, “You have kept us alive, and we have found favor in the sight of our lord. We will be Pharaoh's slaves.”

This was the regulation Joseph established in the land of Egypt, and it has remained in force to this day: they must give Pharaoh a fifth share, down to the present day. The only exception was the priests’ land, which did not become Pharaoh’s.
Israel lived in Goshen, and it became their allotted land. They multiplied and became very numerous.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years. The years of Jacob’s life were one hundred and forty-seven years.

When the time for Israel to die drew near, he called his son Joseph and said to him, “If I have found favor in your sight, put your hand on my body and show me kindness and faithfulness: do not bury me in Egypt.”
“But let me sleep with my fathers. Take me out of the land of Egypt and bury me in my fathers' burial place.” Joseph said to him, “Yes, I will do as you have said.”
He said to him, “Swear to me.” And he swore to me. Israel bowed down at the top of his staff.
After this, they told Joseph, “Our father is ill.” Joseph took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
They told Israel, “Look, your son Joseph is coming to you.” Israel gathered his strength and sat up on his bed.
Jacob said to Joseph, “My God, who appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
said to me, ‘Look, I will increase you and multiply you, and make you a community of nations. I will give this land to you and to your descendants after you, so that they may possess it forever.’
“Now these two sons of yours, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came here to you, Ephraim and Manasseh, are mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are.
“If you have any children from now on, they will bear their brothers’ names and be named after them, and they will share in their brothers’ inheritance.

“When I came from Syrian Mesopotamia, Rachel your mother died in the land of Canaan, as I approached the horse-racing course in the region of Ephrathah, on the way to Ephrathah. I buried her along the road by the horse-racing course called Bethlehem.”
When Israel saw Joseph’s sons, he said to him, “Who are these to you?”
Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” Jacob said to him, “Bring them to me so that I may bless them.”
Israel’s eyes had grown heavy and clouded with age, and he could not open them and see. He brought them close to him, and he kissed and embraced them.
Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I have not been separated from your presence, and now God has shown me your descendants as well.”
Joseph brought them out from between his knees and bowed down before him with his face to the ground.
Joseph took both his sons and placed Ephraim at his right, toward Israel’s left, and Manasseh at his left, toward Israel’s right. He brought them close to his father.
Israel stretched out his right hand and placed it on Ephraim's head, though he was younger than his brother. He placed his left hand on Manasseh's head, crossing his hands.
He blessed them and said, “The God whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac pleased in his presence, the God who has cared for me and fed me from my youth until now, to this very day—

And may the angel of God, who rescued me from every evil, bless these children. May my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac be carried on through them. May they increase and multiply and fill the earth.
And when Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head and his left on Manasseh’s head,
Joseph said to his father, “Not like this, Father, for this one is my firstborn. Put your right hand on him.”

He said to him, “I know, my son, I know. This one too will become a people, and this one too will become great. But his younger brother will become greater than he, and his offspring will become many nations.”
He blessed them that day and said, “Through you Israel will pronounce blessings, saying, ‘May God bless you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’”
Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I am dying, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.”
“Look, I give you fine spoil, better than your brothers' share, which I took from the hands of the Amorites with my bow and my spear.”
Jacob called his sons and said to them, “Gather together, and I will tell you what will happen to you in the days to come.”
Jacob’s sons gathered together and came, and he said to them, “Listen to your father.”
Reuben, my firstborn, is mighty, and my first son became wicked. He stiffened his neck and did dreadful things.
He froze like water, because he went up onto your father’s bed, and you defiled that bed on which he went up.
Simeon and Levi are brothers. They carried out injustice with their [?] and their spears.
May my soul not join them or enter their turmoil, for in their wrath they killed people, and at their pleasure they cut the sinews of cities.
Cursed be their wrath, for they did not [?] their anger. I will divide them within Jacob and scatter them within Israel.
Judah, your brothers have praised you. Your hands are on the backs of your enemies. Your father’s sons will bow down to you.
Judah is a lion’s cub. Rise from your prey, my son. You lay down and slept like a lion and like a lion’s cub; there is no one who will awaken you.
Kingship will not disappear from Judah, nor rule from his offspring, until what is reserved for him arrives. He is the hope of the nations.
He will tie his foal in a vineyard and his donkey to an olive tree. He will wash his clothes in wine and his linen garment in the blood of grapes.
His eyes are joyful from wine, and his teeth are white as milk.
Zebulun [?] will dwell like a harbor for ships, and he will extend as far as Sidon.
Issachar loved what was good and will rest between allotted lands.
When he saw that rest was good, he lowered his shoulders in servitude to the land, took up the yoke, and became a farmer.
Dan will judge his people like one of the tribes of Israel.
Let Dan be a serpent of the earth, lying in wait on the road, biting a horse’s heels so that its rider falls backward.
He will wait for God to save him.
Raiders raided Gad, and he in turn raided them, following their tracks.
Asher is full of grain, and he will give food to angels.
Naphtali is a plant of rest that produces beautiful fruit.
Joseph is a son who grows great, my son who surpasses me and is jealous of me, my young son who returns to me.
Those who attacked him with their schemes became his adversaries and struck him.
Their bows were shattered by force, and the sinews of their forearms grew weak by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob. There he strengthened Israel, with the help of your father's God.
My God helped you and blessed you with the blessing of heaven above and the blessing of the earth, which has everything in it, because of the blessing of breasts and wombs.

The blessing of your father and mother is stronger than the blessing of the mountains that are beloved through the blessing of God's angels. May it rest on Joseph's head and on the heads of those who became his brothers.
Benjamin is a ravenous wolf. He eats in the morning, and toward evening he gives food.
These are the twelve sons of Jacob, and this is what their father told them. Their father blessed them, blessing each one according to his own blessing.
He said to them, “Look, I am going to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
in the double cave opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite, which he bought as a burial place.
There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife, and there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife, and there they buried Leah,
in the cave in the field that they bought from the descendants of Heth.”
Jacob finished giving instructions to his sons, stretched out his feet on his bed, and died. They buried him with his people.
Joseph fell upon his father's face and wept over him.
Joseph ordered his servants who attended him, the embalmers, to embalm his father. The embalmers embalmed Israel.
They completed forty days for them, for that is how they count the days spent embalming. The Egyptians mourned for seventy days.
After the days of mourning were over, Joseph said to Pharaoh's officials, “If I have found favor in your sight, speak to Pharaoh on my behalf and tell him,
‘Before he died, my father made me swear an oath and said to me, “Bury me there, in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now let me go up and bury my father, and I will return.’”
Pharaoh said to him, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear.”
Joseph went up to bury his father. All Pharaoh's sons went up with him, and all the great men of Egypt went up,
along with everyone in Joseph's household, his brothers, everyone in his father's household, and his relatives. But they left their sheep and cattle in the land of Goshen.
Chariots and horses went up with him, and their procession was very large.
They reached the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan. They wept for him with great and very bitter weeping, and they mourned their father for seven days.

The inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad and said, “This is a great mourning of the Egyptians.” Because of this, they named the place “Mourning of Egypt,” which is beyond the Jordan.
His sons did this for him and buried him there.
His sons brought him back to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave that Abraham had bought as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.
Joseph returned to Egypt, he and all those with him who had gone up together to bury their father, and his brothers as well.
Then, when his brothers saw that their father had died, they said, “Perhaps Joseph will remember against us the evil we did to him and repay us for all the evil we showed him.”
Joseph’s brothers came to him and said, “Before he died, your father solemnly made us swear an oath.

He said, ‘Say this to Joseph: Forgive their wrongdoing and their offenses, for they did evil to you. And now, by their God, the God of your fathers, forgive the sins of your servants.’” Joseph wept as they spoke to him.
They came to him and said, “Here we are; we have become your servants.”
Joseph said to them, “Do not be afraid, for I belong to God.
You planned evil against me, but God planned good for me, so that things would be as they are today, with many people being fed.”
He said to them, “Do not be afraid. I will provide food for you and your households.” He called them and spoke words that reached their hearts.
Joseph remained in Egypt, together with his brothers and his father’s entire household. Joseph lived for one hundred and ten years.
Joseph saw Ephraim's descendants to the third generation, and the children of Machir, Manasseh's son, who were born on Joseph's lap.
Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying. And when God visits you and brings you out of this land into the land that God swore to our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—”
Joseph made the children of Israel swear an oath and said to them, “When God visits you, take my bones up from here with you.”
Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They buried him and placed him in a coffin in the land of Egypt.
